tools.name: eslint_check
tools.description: ESLint code quality check (dry-run). Returns violations. Runs in Storefront context. Routes each path to the app tree (eslint:app) or the components tree (eslint:components) and runs both when both are targeted.

project_root.description: Absolute path to a linked git worktree of the root this server was launched in. The call runs against that tree. Omit to use the sticky root set by set_project_root, or the launch root when none is set. Works in every environment: the call runs against that tree as the server's environment reaches it, and under docker, docker-compose, vagrant and ddev the worktree must sit inside the launch project root, which is the only tree the container or VM mounts.

paths.description: File paths or directories to lint. Three forms are accepted per path: repo-root-relative ("src/Storefront/Resources/views/components/..." or "src/Storefront/Resources/app/storefront/..."), tree-relative ("views/components/..." for the components tree, "src/..." or "build/..." for the app tree), and a path already carrying the package prefix. A path containing "views/components/" is linted as a component; everything else as app code. Omit to lint both trees via lint:js.

output_format.description: ESLint output format. Applied only when paths are supplied.

scope.description: Scope name from .mcp-js-tooling.json. Omit to use the configured default_scope. Pass "shopware" to force project-root behavior.

tools.name: jest_run
tools.description: Jest test runner for the Storefront app/storefront package suite only (rootDir is that package, testMatch collects **/test/**/*.test.js). Component tests under views/components/ are not collected by Jest — run those with vitest_run. Returns test results, preceded by a summary line with the test and suite counts. Pass/fail is derived from Jest's own JSON report, not from the process exit code: a run whose tests all passed but whose process exited non-zero afterwards is reported as a pass with the exit code called out, and a run that matched no test is reported as an error rather than a pass.

project_root.description: Absolute path to a linked git worktree of the root this server was launched in. The call runs against that tree. Omit to use the sticky root set by set_project_root, or the launch root when none is set. Works in every environment: the call runs against that tree as the server's environment reaches it, and under docker, docker-compose, vagrant and ddev the worktree must sit inside the launch project root, which is the only tree the container or VM mounts.

testPathPatterns.description: Regex pattern for test file paths (--testPathPatterns). Patterns targeting views/components/ are rejected; use vitest_run instead.

ci.description: Run Jest in CI mode (--ci). Defaults to false. Turning it on stops Jest writing snapshots that do not exist yet, which it would otherwise do by default. It does not cancel out "updateSnapshots": passing that resolves the snapshot mode to "all" whether or not CI mode is on, so snapshots are still written. Coverage is unaffected: the Storefront Jest config collects it unconditionally. Leave it off unless you need CI-identical behavior.

tools.name: set_project_root
tools.description: Set the project root every later call on this server targets, or clear it. Pass a linked git worktree of the root the server was launched in to move the server onto that tree; omit project_root to return it to the launch root. Each of php-tooling, js-admin-tooling and js-storefront-tooling is a separate process and keeps its own setting, so call this on each server you use.

project_root.description: Absolute path to a linked git worktree of the root this server was launched in. Omit to clear the setting and return the server to its launch root; the value being discarded is not validated, so this also recovers from a worktree that has been removed. Works in every environment: the call runs against that tree as the server's environment reaches it, and under docker, docker-compose, vagrant and ddev the worktree must sit inside the launch project root, which is the only tree the container or VM mounts.

tools.name: cwd
tools.description: Report where this server resolves to: the effective project root and whether it came from set_project_root or from the launch, whether that root still resolves, the working directory, the environment, and the configuration files in use. Takes no parameters. Validates nothing and never fails, so it also reports a project root that has been removed.
